chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, concerning:
A man performing wudu (ablution) with the leftover water of a menstruating woman. He عليه السلام said: If she is trustworthy, then there is no harm.

key_terms.فَضْلِ: leftover remainder, meaning the water remaining after someone has used it
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةً: trustworthy, considered reliable regarding purity and cleanliness

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform wudu with the leftover water of a menstruating woman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding wudu (ablution) with water left over by a menstruating woman. It states that if she is considered trustworthy, there is no problem in using that water, indicating its permissibility in the context of ritual purity.
